hypotheses.justification: Implied by hw, hθ and hprime. `w : v.Extension (𝓞 L)` means `w.1.under (𝓞 K) = v`, so hw says w is unramified over v. The file proves `isField_V` from hw alone: V = k_v ⊗ O_w is a field of degree d = [L_w:K_v] over k_v, so the local extension is unramified with residue degree d. By hθ, θ has order d ≥ |Aut(L_w/K_v)|, so L_w/K_v is Galois (cyclic) with group generated by θ. In an unramified Galois extension the inertia group is trivial, so reduction is an isomorphism Gal(L_w/K_v) ≅ Gal(k_w/k_v), and θ maps to θ̄ of order d. Since d is prime (hprime), d ≥ 2 and θ̄ ≠ 1. Pick ȳ with θ̄ȳ ≠ ȳ and lift it to y ∈ O_w: then ‖y‖ ≤ 1, and θy − y is integral but not in the maximal ideal, hence a unit, so ‖θy − y‖ = 1. In the proof, hres is only used to get `sigmaV_ne_one`, which this argument supplies; the rest of the proof is unchanged.

The proof uses hprime only for d > 0 (`hprime.pos`) and to get `orderOf_sigmaV` through `orderOf_eq_prime`. First, d > 0 holds anyway because L_w/K_v is finite-dimensional. Second, orderOf σ = d holds without primality. hθ makes L_w/K_v Galois with group ⟨θ⟩, and hw (via `isField_V`) makes it unramified. Then O_w = O_v[α] with α lifting a generator of the residue extension, and the minimal polynomial of α has separable reduction (finite fields). So θ^k(α) ≡ α mod ϖ forces θ^k(α) = α, i.e. θ^k = id. Hence σ^k ≠ 1 for 0 < k < d, and σ^d = 1 by `sigmaV_pow_finrank`. With orderOf σ = d, the rest of `finrank_ker_le_one` (fixed field of ⟨σ⟩ is k_v, Hilbert-90 style kernel bound) and the rest of the proof go through unchanged. Degenerate cases: hres forces θ ≠ id, so d ≥ 2; and in the d = 1 case the formula q^{min(s,m)} can be checked directly. Each of hres and hprime is claimed deletable on its own (the other kept); deleting both together was not checked.
